research_question: What is the effect of a fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy combination, compared with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, on overall survival in adults with advanced pancreatic cancer?
outcome_description: Overall survival (OS) evaluated via time-to-event survival analysis (Cox proportional hazards model)
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates improved overall survival (longer survival duration / reduced mortality risk) favoring the fluoropyrimidine-based combination regimen over gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel.
search_queries: fluoropyrimidine gemcitabine nab-paclitaxel pancreatic cancer trial
fluoropyrimidine combination gemcitabine nab-paclitaxel advanced pancreatic survival
FOLFIRINOX or S-1 gemcitabine nab-paclitaxel pancreatic adenocarcinoma randomized
inclusion_criteria: Adult patients (aged 18 or older) with advanced, locally advanced, or metastatic pancreatic cancer.
Comparative studies evaluating a fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy regimen against gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel.
Reporting quantitative overall survival data derived from time-to-event survival analysis.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, conference abstracts without data, editorials, commentaries, and narrative reviews are excluded).

No comparison between a fluoropyrimidine-based combination regimen and gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (e.g. trials comparing different doses or schedules of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel against each other, or comparisons with best supportive care, gemcitabine monotherapy, or fluoropyrimidine monotherapy).
No quantitative time-to-event overall survival outcome data usable to derive an effect size (lacking hazard ratios, risk ratios with confidence intervals, or Cox survival model outputs).
Completely unrelated to advanced pancreatic cancer or chemotherapy interventions.
moderators_to_extract: Specific fluoropyrimidine regimen (e.g., FOLFIRINOX/mFOLFIRINOX, S-1 plus nab-paclitaxel, capecitabine combinations)
Line of therapy (first-line vs second-line or subsequent)
Study design (randomized controlled trial vs prospective comparative cohort)
Geographic region / study population (e.g., East Asia vs North America/Europe)
Disease stage distribution (percentage of metastatic vs locally advanced disease)
effect_size_note: Extract Risk Ratio (RR) or Hazard Ratio (HR) with 95% confidence interval or log-hazard ratio and standard error directly from Cox proportional hazards / time-to-event survival analysis for overall survival.
